Restaurant GST Billing Guide: Complete GST Compliance for Restaurants

Everything you need to know about GST for restaurants in India - rates, invoicing, compliance, input tax credit, and how restaurant POS software simplifies GST compliance.

By NexDine Team•June 20, 2024•10 min read

Understanding GST for Restaurants in India

Goods and Services Tax (GST) has transformed how restaurants handle taxation in India. Since its implementation in 2017, restaurant owners have had to adapt to new compliance requirements, invoicing standards, and tax calculation methods. This guide covers everything you need to know about GST for restaurants, from rates and compliance to how restaurant POS software can simplify the process.

GST Rates for Restaurants

GST rates for restaurants vary based on the type of establishment and annual turnover. Understanding which rate applies to your restaurant is crucial for compliance and accurate billing.

Restaurants with Turnover Up to ₹40 Lakhs

Small restaurants with annual turnover up to ₹40 lakhs can opt for the composition scheme under GST. Under this scheme:

  • Charge a flat 5% GST on food and beverages
  • Cannot claim input tax credit (ITC)
  • File quarterly returns instead of monthly
  • Simplified compliance requirements

This scheme is ideal for small restaurants, cafes, and eateries that want simplified compliance. However, the inability to claim ITC may not be beneficial if your restaurant has significant input taxes.

Restaurants with Turnover Above ₹40 Lakhs

Restaurants with annual turnover above ₹40 lakhs must register under regular GST and charge:

  • 5% GST on food and beverages (non-AC restaurants)
  • 18% GST on food and beverages (AC restaurants or those serving alcohol)
  • 18% GST on outdoor catering services
  • Can claim input tax credit on purchases
  • Must file monthly returns

Special Cases

Certain restaurant types have specific GST considerations:

  • Room service in hotels: If room service is provided without a separate restaurant, it's taxed at the hotel's GST rate (typically 18%)
  • Restaurants in hotels: If the restaurant has a separate billing counter, restaurant GST rates apply. If billing is through the hotel, hotel GST rates apply
  • Cafeterias in institutions: May be exempt if providing subsidized food to employees
  • Cloud kitchens: Same GST rates as regular restaurants based on AC/non-AC status

GST Invoicing Requirements for Restaurants

GST invoices must meet specific requirements to be compliant. Restaurant POS software like NexDine automatically generates compliant invoices, but understanding the requirements helps ensure accuracy.

Mandatory Invoice Fields

Every GST invoice must include:

  • Invoice number (serially numbered)
  • Date of issue
  • Name, address, and GSTIN of the supplier
  • Name and address of the recipient (if registered)
  • Recipient's GSTIN (if registered)
  • HSN/SAC code of goods/services
  • Description of goods/services
  • Taxable value
  • GST rate (CGST, SGST, or IGST)
  • Tax amount (CGST, SGST, or IGST)
  • Total invoice value
  • Signature or digital signature

Invoice Copies

GST invoices must be issued in triplicate:

  • Original copy: For the buyer
  • Duplicate copy: For the transporter (if goods are transported)
  • Triplicate copy: For the seller's record

For services (like restaurant dining), duplicate and triplicate copies may not be required, but maintaining records is essential for audit purposes.

Input Tax Credit (ITC) for Restaurants

Input tax credit allows restaurants to offset GST paid on purchases against GST collected on sales. This is a significant benefit that reduces the overall tax burden.

What Can Be Claimed as ITC

Restaurants can claim ITC on:

  • Raw materials and ingredients
  • Kitchen equipment and appliances
  • Furniture and fixtures
  • Service charges paid to suppliers
  • Rent (if GST is paid)
  • Utilities (electricity, water if GST applies)
  • Marketing and advertising services
  • Professional services (accounting, legal)

What Cannot Be Claimed as ITC

ITC cannot be claimed on:

  • Motor vehicles (except specific cases)
  • Food and beverages for employee consumption
  • Membership fees of clubs
  • Works contract services for construction of immovable property
  • Goods or services used for personal consumption

ITC Restrictions for Restaurants

Important restrictions to note:

  • Restaurants under composition scheme cannot claim ITC
  • ITC must be claimed within the relevant financial year or before filing annual return
  • ITC is blocked if supplier has not paid GST to the government
  • Proper documentation (tax invoices) is required to claim ITC

GST Returns Filing for Restaurants

Restaurants must file various GST returns based on their turnover and registration type. Missing deadlines can result in penalties and interest charges.

GSTR-1

Details of outward supplies (sales):

  • Due date: 11th of the following month
  • Contains invoice details, customer GSTIN, tax collected
  • Required for all regular GST registered restaurants
  • Composition scheme restaurants file GSTR-4 instead

GSTR-3B

Summary return with tax payment:

  • Due date: 20th of the following month
  • Contains summary of sales, purchases, ITC, and tax payment
  • Self-assessment return
  • Required for all regular GST registered restaurants

GSTR-4

Return for composition scheme taxpayers:

  • Due date: 18th of the month following the quarter
  • Contains summary of supplies and tax paid
  • Required for restaurants under composition scheme

GSTR-9

Annual return:

  • Due date: December 31st of the following financial year
  • Contains consolidated summary of all returns filed during the year
  • Required for all GST registered businesses

Best Practices for Restaurant GST Compliance

Follow these best practices to ensure smooth GST compliance:

1. Maintain Proper Records

Keep all invoices, purchase records, and tax documents organized. Restaurant POS software maintains digital records automatically, making record retrieval easy during audits.

2. Reconcile ITC Regularly

Reconcile ITC claimed with GSTR-2A data monthly. Identify discrepancies early and take corrective action to avoid ITC denial.

3. File Returns on Time

Late filing attracts penalties and interest. Set reminders and use restaurant POS software compliance alerts to never miss a deadline.

4. Stay Updated on GST Changes

GST regulations change periodically. Stay informed about rate changes, compliance updates, and new requirements. Restaurant POS software providers typically update systems to reflect changes.

5. Use Technology

Leverage restaurant POS software to automate GST processes. Manual compliance is inefficient and error-prone. Technology ensures accuracy and saves valuable time.

Common GST Mistakes to Avoid

Avoid these common GST mistakes that restaurants make:

1. Incorrect GST Rate Application

Applying the wrong GST rate is a common error. Ensure your restaurant POS software is configured with correct rates for different items and service types.

2. Missing ITC Claims

Failing to claim eligible ITC results in higher tax liability. Track all purchases and claim ITC within the allowed timeframe.

3. Late Return Filing

Late filing attracts late fees and interest. Use compliance alerts and calendar reminders to file on time.

4. Incomplete Invoice Details

Incomplete invoices can be rejected during audits. Ensure all mandatory fields are included in every invoice.

5. Not Maintaining Records

Poor record-keeping makes compliance difficult and audit-proofing impossible. Use restaurant POS software to maintain comprehensive digital records.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the GST rate for restaurants in India?

Restaurant GST rates vary based on the type of establishment. Restaurants with turnover up to ₹40 lakhs are exempt from GST (composition scheme). Restaurants with turnover above ₹40 lakhs charge 5% GST on food and beverages. AC restaurants and those serving alcohol charge 18% GST. Outdoor catering charges 18% GST.

How does restaurant POS software help with GST compliance?

Restaurant POS software like NexDine automates GST calculations, generates GST-compliant invoices, tracks input tax credit, maintains GST-ready reports, and ensures accurate tax collection. This reduces manual errors, saves time, and ensures compliance with GST regulations.

What is input tax credit (ITC) for restaurants?

Input tax credit allows restaurants to claim credit for GST paid on purchases like ingredients, equipment, and services. Restaurants can offset this credit against their GST liability. However, restaurants under the composition scheme cannot claim ITC. Proper tracking of ITC requires maintaining detailed purchase records.

What are the GST invoicing requirements for restaurants?

GST invoices must include GSTIN of both parties, invoice number, date, HSN/SAC codes, taxable value, GST rate, and tax amount. Invoices must be serially numbered and issued in triplicate for supply of goods. Restaurant POS software automatically generates compliant invoices with all required fields.

How often do restaurants need to file GST returns?

Restaurants with turnover above ₹40 lakhs must file GSTR-1 monthly (by 11th of next month) and GSTR-3B monthly (by 20th of next month). Restaurants under composition scheme file GSTR-4 quarterly. Annual return GSTR-9 is due by December 31st of the following year.
